newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- NEW ISSUES SEEN OFFERING VALUE.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- NEW ISSUES SEEN OFFERING VALUE.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds firmed about an eighth of a point in early afternoon trade on Friday, lifted by Treasuries, but the spotlight was on new issues, with some selling briskly because they were seen as bargains.

For example, there was speculation that Denver Airport, which sold $371 million of bonds with at top yield of 5.60 percent in 2025 through Goldman, Sachs, might reprice the offering by raising rates five basis points.
"I think the deal's a riot...It's oversubscribed," a Midwest trader said. "The buyers think the levels are too cheap," he added.

Another trader said the the State of New York Metropolitan Transportation Authority, which sold $227 million of revenue bonds at a top yield of 5.56 percent in 2027 through Smith Barney, also appeared to have given buyers a bit of an opportunity.

"I certainly wouldn't call it rich, I wouldn't say it's priced to sell, it's better than being on the market," a trader said. The Authority also sold $165 million of bonds with a top yield of 5.625 percent in 2027.
However, the secondary market did not capture the same buying interest, partly because it has failed to match all of the slim recovery staged by Treasury bonds since Friday's huge sell-off.
"The secondary market has not adjusted the same step-for-step with governments," a trader said.
Actively traded issues included E-470 Public Highway Authority Colorado Revenues of 2021, which pay a five percent coupon, and were bid at 5.49 percent, NET, down two basis points.
And Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority bonds of 2024, which carry a five percent coupon, were bid at 5.54 percent, NET, down one basis point.

Treasury bond futures were buoyed by a few signs of slowing wage inflation pressures and the possibility manufacturing was slipping in the Southeast, though the latter report was attributed to seasonal factors.
The second quarter 2.4 percent unit labor cost increase was below forecasts of 2.7 percent.
The Richmond Federal Reserve shipments index for July fell to minus 10 from plus 15 in June. The new orders index as seven, down from June's reading of 11.

However, an official at the Richmond Federal Reserve said the drop in shipments was seasonal, adding economic activity in the District of Columbia, Maryland, North Carolina, South Carolina, Virginia and most of West Virginia, appeared fairly robust in the third quarter, with broad-based, underlying strength.

In Chicago futures markets, September municipal bond futures gained seven ticks to 119-6/32, while September Treasury bond futures climbed 11 ticks to 113-4/32. This left the MOB spread at plus 195 ticks.
